_readme: Prompts for tools/illustrate.mjs. Edit freely — this is the writing, not the code.
style     prepended to every prompt, so the whole book looks like one book
sheet     generate this one first; it exists to be used as a reference
ref       the id of a sheet to hand the model along with the prompt
Prompts are in English because the model follows English art direction more
reliably. Nothing here contains a real person's name or details — the girl in
these pictures is נחל, the character.
style: Children's book illustration for ages 8-10. Soft 3D clay-render look: rounded, chunky shapes with gentle depth, as if modelled in plasticine and lit from the upper left. Warm night palette — deep indigo and teal shadows, soft cream and amber highlights. Painterly, cosy, a little theatrical. No text, no letters, no words anywhere in the image. Composed with clear empty space so the picture reads small on a phone.
negative: Do not include any text, captions, letters, numbers, watermarks, logos or signatures. Avoid photorealism, harsh contrast, scary or threatening imagery.

illustrations.prompt: Character sheet, three views on a plain warm background: a nine-year-old girl called Nachal, standing, three-quarter view, and a close-up of her face. Curly dark brown hair tied back but escaping, olive skin, wide curious brown eyes, a permanent half-smile like she is about to say something. Mustard-yellow jumper, denim dungarees, one red sneaker and one blue sneaker. She carries a battered notebook under one arm. Energetic posture, never still.

Character sheet, two views on a plain warm background: a nine-year-old girl called Tamar. Straight black hair in a blunt bob, round glasses, calm deadpan expression, very upright posture. Green jumper, grey skirt, high socks. She is holding a green fabric dragon tail in one hand as if it were perfectly normal.

Character sheet of Mr Pip, an elderly short stage manager, on a plain warm background. Round friendly face, half-moon glasses, and an extraordinarily long white moustache whose ends are tied together behind his ears. Waistcoat over a rumpled shirt, sleeves rolled, a hammer in one pocket and a mug in his hand. Kind, unhurried, slightly rumpled.

Nachal alone in the third row of a small empty old theatre, looking up at a heavy sunset-coloured stage curtain that is very slightly moving. Rows of red seats, warm dusty light from a single stage lamp, deep shadows in the wings. She is leaning forward, notebook forgotten on her knees.

A narrow storeroom lined with wooden shelves, crowded with glass jars. Inside each jar floats a small drifting light in a different colour — amber, pink, pale green, blue. On the top shelf sits a very small creature wearing a coat sewn from strips of paper, with a pair of closed scissors on its head like a pointed hat. Cosy and strange rather than frightening.

Two girls taking a bow on a small theatre stage, lit warm amber. One wears paper dragon wings; the other has her arms spread wide like a butterfly. Beside them stands a kettle wearing a crown on a stool, and a wooden toy duck on wheels. Long strands of imaginary spaghetti are draped everywhere. The front row of the audience is a blur of laughing faces. Joyful, chaotic, the best night of the year.

A narrow alley behind a theatre at dusk. A squat old green postbox, about as tall as a child, with a slot in its side and a heavy iron crank handle like a mincer. Paint peeling. Nachal is turning the handle with both hands and her whole body; Tamar watches with her arms folded. A single white envelope is emerging from the slot.

A tiny sorting room the size of a broom cupboard, lit by one bare bulb. A wooden sorting table, three deep drawers, and a huge heap of unopened envelopes piled across the floor, each stamped with a red mark. Nachal stands knee-deep in the heap holding one envelope up to the light. Dust in the air.

Close view of three wooden drawers in a row, freshly labelled with hand-written paper tags in a child's handwriting, pulled slightly open. Neat stacks of sorted envelopes inside. A wooden toy duck on wheels sits on top of the cabinet, facing the viewer. Warm lamplight, calm and satisfying.

A vast painted canvas backdrop unrolled across a stage floor, showing a whole painted city: rooftops, staircases, washing lines, a cat on a railing, one window with a warm light on. In the lower right corner of the canvas there is a conspicuously blank square of bare cloth. Nachal is kneeling at the edge of the canvas, small against it, looking at the empty corner.

Night in a dark theatre. A single shaft of light falls on the lower corner of a huge painted backdrop. From the shadows at the edge of the frame reaches one very old hand, covered in permanent paint stains, holding a rag. Tense and quiet, not frightening — the hand is hesitant, not grasping.

Close view of the corner of a painted canvas, lit by a work lamp. A child's paintbrush rests against it. Beside it stands a very small, very old painter with enormous paint-stained hands, looking at the corner. Nachal stands next to him holding a jar of water. Quiet, warm, a little solemn.

A child alone in the centre of a bare stage under a single warm spotlight, seen from the back of the empty auditorium. Nachal stands with her arms held slightly away from her sides, clearly trying very hard not to move. A big wall clock is visible at the edge of the frame. Funny and tender rather than tense.

Nachal sitting in the third row of a dark auditorium, cross-legged on the seat, an open notebook on her knees and a heavy old brass stopwatch on a chain held up in one hand. The stage beyond her is lit amber and empty. She looks completely in charge.

Two girls standing on a stage in low amber light. One holds up a small lantern that lights both their faces from below; the other stands two steps behind her, saying nothing. The auditorium beyond is dark and completely still. Warm, hushed, the best moment of the evening.
